channel.title: Salt Lake Tribune - Article Feed
channel.description: Latest articles from Salt Lake Tribune (sltrib.com)

item.title: Letter: New Utah Supreme Court appointees should be as highly qualified as current justices
item.description: Letter: Our current Utah Supreme Court justices are highly qualified. If Gov. Cox wants to convince us that adding two justices wasn't about packing the court, he must ensure the new members are highly qualified, too.

item.title: Letter: Donald J. Trump and Martin Luther King: Two peas in a peace pod?
item.description: Letter: Martin Luther King once said world leaders often exercise “power without compassion” and “might without morality.” Is there a better description of Donald Trump than that?

item.title: Letter: Trump’s assault on voters’ rights is well under way. When we lose our vote, we have lost it all.
item.description: Letter: We can no longer call ourselves “the land of the free.” We have sold our self-respect and lost the respect of the rest of the world in the process.

item.title: Gordon Monson: With just one more move, the Utah Jazz can end their nightmare
item.description: The Utah Jazz acquired an All-Star this week. Now they have to work to hold onto their lottery pick.

item.title: A minor earthquake, centered in Utah County, rattles the Wasatch Front
item.description: People along the Wasatch Front reported feeling the rattles of an earthquake Thursday afternoon. The epicenter was in Utah County.

item.title: LDS Church can continue construction of Heber Valley Temple, Utah Supreme Court rules
item.description: A lawsuit filed by Wasatch County residents has stifled construction on The Church of Jesus Christ of Latter-day Saints' Heber Valley Temple for years. On Thursday, the Utah Supreme Court ruled the church can continue building.

item.description: Check out Pat Bagley's latest cartoon: Beat the Press

item.title: SLC Council member ‘cannot imagine even ceding an inch’ on traffic-calming in face of new bill
item.description: For the second straight year, Utah lawmakers are looking to restrict where and how Salt Lake City officials can slow down cars on city streets.

item.title: SLC approves ‘historic’ union pact with its library workers
item.description: The Salt Lake City library is being billed as the state's first to unionize.

item.title: Utahns take to the streets outside of BYU to protest Border Patrol’s presence at campus job fair
item.description: Border Patrol's inclusion at a BYU job fair sparks protests off campus, with some demonstrators saying the immigration crackdown doesn't fit with LDS Church principles.
